content.theory:
Strings hold text. You can create them with single or double quotes:

```python
city = 'Delhi'
country = "India"
```

Strings have useful **methods** — functions that belong to the string:

```python
text = "Hello, World"
print(text.upper())     # HELLO, WORLD
print(text.lower())     # hello, world
print(text.strip())     # removes surrounding spaces
print(text.replace("World", "Python"))  # Hello, Python
print(len(text))        # 12 — length of the string
```

**Slicing** lets you grab parts of a string using `[start:end]`:

```python
print(text[0:5])   # Hello
print(text[7:])    # World
print(text[-5:])   # World (last 5 chars)
```

**Concatenation** joins strings with `+`:

```python
first = "Sam"
last = "Lee"
full = first + " " + last
```

`len()` works on strings — but returns the number of characters, so `len("hello")` is `5`.
